about: The g-motions as motions, not as jumps: `gg` under an operator (`dgg`), and `gg` extending a visual selection (`vgg`). Measured 2026-11-13: vim and busybox both support `dgg`; nvi does not (it is modern-vim lineage), and neither nvi nor busybox does the visual form, so those cases are vim-only. Both broke in the same way marks once did: `gg` existed only as a cursor move, so a pending operator was dropped and the cursor moved instead of deleting. `Gdgg` is vim-only: busybox reports the surviving empty line as a newline where vim normalises it away - the same buffer in two reporting conventions.

cases.name: dgg deletes back to the top of the buffer
dgg from the second line deletes one line
vgg extends the selection to the top and d takes it
gg in visual mode moves the head, so the selection collapses to line 1
